resources.string: The Steam account GamePort uses for the library, downloads and game identity.

This deletes everything GamePort keeps for this account: the saved session, the game list and any unfinished downloads. Games already installed stay on this device until they are uninstalled. A new QR code scan is needed to sign back in.
What every game uses when seated mode is on. A game that has its own setting keeps it.
Each game can override this from its own settings, and go back to this value with one button.
Shows the artwork of the selected game behind the library.
The language of the app. Automatic follows the language of this device.
Lower: darker and blurrier behind the library. Higher: clearer.
Shows the name of each game at the bottom of its cover.
Full: the cover zooms and a ring drifts out around it. Reduced: no zoom or drift. None: the ring just appears.
What the home shows above and between the rows of covers. Each can be switched off to keep the page light.
The games marked with a star.
Hide games that are not installed
Only the games ready to play are listed.
The colour of buttons, switches and the ring around a highlighted cover. The rainbow circle picks any other colour.
Name pill on the highlighted cover
A pill with the name of the game and a play icon appears above the cover being pointed at; pressing it starts the game. Off: the room kept for it above the covers is removed.
The size of the name above the highlighted cover, and the room kept for it.
The gradient behind every page, also shown for games without artwork. Pick a pair, or each end with the circles.
Every appearance setting goes back to its default.
Every home setting goes back to its default.
All: the VR and the flat games started most recently. Shown tab: only those of the tab selected, VR or Flat.

Achievements unlocked in a game are added to the Steam account, and the ones the account already has (earned on a PC, for example) are given to the game when it starts. This writes to the account and GamePort cannot take an achievement back. Only achievements unlocked while this is on are sent, and one that cannot be sent right away waits for a connection.

While a game is on screen, Steam is told the account is playing it, so its time counts on the account. Steam allows one game at a time: starting a game here interrupts one running on another device. Time while the device is asleep or the game is not on screen is not counted.
Come back to GamePort when a game closes

Chooses for which games GamePort opens again once the game is closed. A game started from the headset\'s library otherwise leaves GamePort running in the background, without its screen. A game patched before needs to be patched again to follow a change.
GamePort can look for a newer version of itself. A new version is only downloaded and installed after a tap on the update button, and Android asks for a confirmation.
No check has been made yet.
GamePort is up to date. Last check: %1$s.
The check failed. Is this device connected to the internet?
The download did not finish. It can be started again.
Not enough free space to download the update.
This file is not signed like the installed GamePort and was not installed.
The update could not be installed.
This is a development build: it cannot be replaced by a release. Releases are installed on the normal build only.
A game is being downloaded, patched or installed. The update waits until it is done, and games cannot be installed while GamePort updates.
Saves are being synchronised. The update waits until it is done.
Games patched by an older version: %1$d. Patching them again brings the latest features.
All the games are up to date.
Look for updates when GamePort opens

GamePort looks at the latest release page on GitHub as it opens, if the last look is older than the chosen time. It only looks: nothing is downloaded or installed without a tap on the update button. GitHub can see this device\'s IP address, like for any web page. With Never, updates are only searched with the button above.

GamePort stays off Steam: no connection, no save sync, no play time sent, no download. The library shows what was last saved and installed games still start. Turning it off reconnects. Saves made meanwhile are synced the next time a game starts online.
Games hidden from the app. They stay in the Steam library and nothing changes there.
No game is hidden from the app.

After a game closes, GamePort asks whether it worked. The answer stays on this device, and when this is on it is also sent to the project to show which games work. It carries only the game, the answer, the version of GamePort and the kind of device, with a random number that identifies nobody. No name, address or account. After \"It did not work\" or \"Works offline only\", a technical report is sent too: the versions, files and logs of the game, without any name, e-mail address or account.
Games confirmed as not running through GamePort. They are left out of the home and stay in the Steam library, where nothing changes.
Puts these games back on the home to try them. They may close by themselves.
No game of the library is confirmed as incompatible.
How much of the height of a game\'s page its artwork covers. At 0 there is no artwork, at 100 it fills the screen.

The Steam region games are downloaded from. Automatic follows the location of the connection. Another region can be faster on a network whose route to the nearest server is poor. A change reconnects to Steam at once, and a download in progress stops and can be resumed.
Size of the new Android versions
The carousel of the games whose Android version just arrived.
Guided tours, and every label, notice and button of the app explained.
A tour dims the screen and lights each part in turn, with a short explanation. The complete tour goes through every page. It can be left at any time.
Or one page at a time. The pages of a game are shown with made-up values, so every button and notice appears.
On a game\'s page, a label says what players report for the kind of device in use.
Most players who tried the game say it works.
It works for most players, and for at least half of them only with the network off. Turning on the offline mode in Settings > Steam account may be needed.
Opinions are divided: it works for some players and not for others.
Many players had problems. The game can still be installed, after a confirmation.
The game is known not to run. The page says why, in red, and the game is hidden from the home. Settings > Incompatible games lists them.
When few players answered, a note says the result may not be reliable. A game tried with the offline mode says so too.
A notice appears on the page of an installed game only when something applies. Orange and red marks need attention, green is a new version, and blue only informs.
A new version of the game is available. A button updates it.
A newer GamePort patch exists for the game. A button patches it again.
The game closed almost right away or crashed. A button prepares a report that helps find out why.
The game asks for access to files and does not have it, so it may close on its own. A button opens the permission.
The saves on this device and on Steam differ, and a choice is needed between them.
The last save sync did not reach Steam or failed, so the latest saves may not be on Steam.
The game starts but does not seem to react to the controllers. Turning on support for the Steam Frame\'s controls may help.
The game has no controls for the controllers of this device, so the Steam Frame\'s are emulated and can be remapped.
The game has expansion files that an earlier patch named after a raised version. If it does not start, uninstalling it and installing it again fixes that.
They appear next to the install button once the game is installed.
Saves. An orange dot says the saves here and on Steam do not agree.
Report a problem. Prepares a report with the logs of the game, without any name or account.
Compatibility options, in orange. A small dot says GamePort adapted the game by itself.
Controllers. Maps the buttons the game expects onto the controllers of this device.
Controllers in orange: the Steam Frame\'s controls are forced for this game.
Controllers in blue: GamePort set up the Steam Frame\'s controls by itself.
Game settings. Settings kept for this game only.
The options that make a game work, one per game.
Force the detection of the Steam Frame\'s controllers
Useful when the game starts but does not react to the controllers. It changes nothing if the game has no controls for the Steam Frame\'s controllers, and a warning says so when that was seen.
Follow the recentering of the device
Automatic, On or Off. Useful when recentering does not bring the game back in front. Automatic turns it on for a device without a play area.
For a game without controls for this device\'s controllers, each button of the Steam Frame\'s controllers can be moved onto another button.

The arguments Steam lists for starting a game. A plain switch for VR is picked at first, and some games stay on a black screen without it. The others are only offered. Any of them can be picked or not, and a game that does not know an argument ignores it.
A problem with a game is best sent with the report button of its page. For everything else, the project\'s Discord is open to anyone.
The link opens in a browser, and Discord can see this device\'s IP address, like any web page.
Every page also has a question mark button at its top that starts its own tour.

resources.string: Counted: the files of the installed app, its expansion files, and what GamePort keeps for it. What a game keeps for itself, such as its data and caches, is hidden by Android and is not counted.
Removed from this device, with their data: %1$s. Saves already synced with Steam Cloud stay there. Android asks to confirm each one.
Files left behind by a download that stopped. Discarding one frees the space it takes.
The files left by the download of %1$s are deleted. It can be started again from the page of the game.
The game has large files beside its app and GamePort cannot check that they are all there. A button repairs it by downloading them again.
The game itself said that some of its large files are not there, so it cannot load its data. A button repairs it by downloading them again.
